item.title: WV17-A writing struggle
item.description:
I have not written any long post for almost a month as I felt my writing juices were over. I needed to replenish them to start writing but I guess that will take a long time. Meanwhile, I was posting about books and movies, both of which I am consuming a lot nowadays. Even in these posts, I was either feeling that I have not much to write or the topics are not important. Although, I had occasional motivation to write about different topics such as habits, some skills, and running, for an ADHD mind like mine these bursts did not last long. The moment passed so did the energy of writing. It's a pity as at that time I felt those topics were important but once I forgot them, I did not feel their importance that strongly.

It is an irony to write about not writing again and again, repeating myself countless times here, here, and here. A serious reader would not like it. But do I even have a serious reader? (Sorry for you, if you exist).

Dear reader, I guarantee that it is not intentional. I feel that I have important things to say, especially due to my sharp observant nature. But writing them takes time, and after a day I have plethora of new observations and new ideas. The situation is overwhelming when I am not delivering enough but have more ideas, and higher expectations.

Now you might be expecting that finally I will say something wise or entertaining. Nope. I will not. I want to run away in shame, hide my face under the pillow. Like Mariam did when her husband Rashid tried to hit her with leather belt and Laila (the second wife) hold it and snatched it to prevent the violence. Mariam was scared; so am I. That was from a book I am reading, A Thousand Splendid Suns by Khaled Hosseini.

Regardless of me being wise or boring, I want to tell you about one of my recent happy moments. I was using Obsidian for quite some time but a few weeks ago it started throwing error on launch. Using Claude, I understood it was a plugin overload. But I was only using 4-5 community plugins. So I was fed up. I decided to quit Obsidian and make my own writing software where I can save my drafts as well. The best candidate for it was my micro-publishing client. I just needed to work on its writing section. So now I have this amazing personalized writing page where I can write and save the drafts. So cool. I am happy writing this post in my micropub client. This strategy also has reduced the number of steps I need to publish. Often, the draft in Obsidian stays there and gets abandoned. But here I feel motivated to finish a piece of text, otherwise it will be sitting on my a**, forever.

A side note. My AI usage is growing, and I am okay with it. I mostly use it for writing new codes and developing tools which would have taken me months if done without AI.

Time to go now. See you next time.

item.title: WV16-Love vs duty and running dilemma
item.description:
Howdy. That's the first word came to my mind around half an hour before I started writing this word-vomit. I have no idea why but after that I was repeating it many times in my head so that I will not forget to use it.

From past few weeks, I have so many thoughts and that's why I have this urge to write a word-vomit post today. I was thinking about multiple topics to write, including Yoga techniques, and many others which I can not recall at this moment. And yet I have not written a single word. I guess the pressure of writing prevents me to write anything at all. The result is me writing word-vomit post which is less pressurizing.

I came back to Brussels after spending a month with my family and six month old son. It was refreshing and calming, with occasional moments of frustrations. Now, sitting thousands of kilometer far, I miss them. There are at least two category of emotions I feel. The first one is about spending time with my family, and live these moments as much as I can because they will never come back. Time is a bitch.

The second type is about responsibility and bringing food on the table. Right now my wife is on a break from work, and my father's business is not doing very well. So all the earning responsibilities are on my shoulder, and that is stressful. My heart wants me to run away to my family and see my son growing up every day, learning new things. While the responsibility demands me to focus on work. Now you might be thinking why not bring your family to Brussels. Well the answer is longer visa-processing-time about which I do not want to talk as this pisses me off further. So that's the problem I am stuck with.

Writing last two lines almost chocked me from the words. So you can see how frustrating this topic is. I will finish this topic with a line from Game of Thrones said by Maester Aemon:

Love is the bane of honor, the death of duty.

Moving to another topic, running. I like running for improving cardio health but I struggle with the discipline to do it regularly. I can run every day and build a habit to do it regularly but this can also increase the chances of injury. So, I need to take rest day to recover which eventually breaks the habit. It is confusing. I am struggling with it for around six months now. I might need help.

My activity calendar indicates that in past four months the maximum number of runs were in May 2026, exactly nine days. A shame. I expect it to be at least fifteen days. What you can observe from this is the gaps between active (green color) days. When I succeeded in breaking the inertia after rest days, I went for run in following days. However, more often this inertia killed the running streak. So maximum in a week was four, only once.

I need to get ready for office now. So see you next time.

item.title: FreshRSS vs My Own Feed Reader: A fierce competetion
item.description:
We all consume online content by different means. The majority of the people prefer mainstream social media while a small number of people use newsletters or RSS/Atom feeds. I am in the latter group.

Those who are not familiar with RSS feed, please have a look at it here. It is a fantastic way to subscribe and read your favorite articles, news and blogs. You can even subscribe to Youtube channels using feeds. However, to access them you need a feed reader. Thanks to the open source community there are plenty of free options available such as FreshRSS and Miniflux.

My primary feed reader is FreshRSS. Its' not that I am a big fan of it as I regularly experiment with new feed readers. However, in the end I always switch back to FreshRSS. The main reason is that it is (over)loaded with features, which makes it super useful. It allows syncing different devices so I can save articles and keep a record of them to read later on other devices. But at the same time it is full of clutter so my ADHD mind does not like it. Another reason is that reading an article in FreshRSS's native reader, instead of at the author's website, gives me FOMO. I feel I can miss out some unannounced updates on fellow bloggers' websites. Also, it's boring to see new articles always in one design, especially when I can go to their original source. So I am always on a hunt to find a better feed reader.

Recently, I decided to take matters into my hands and write plugins/themes for FreshRSS, or develop an alternative-- my own feed reader. In either case, the main feature I wanted was link aggregation so that I can read a post at its source webpage. However, given my limited programming skills it was an intimidating task. So, I took some help from Claude to test both strategies, and figure out which one would be best for me.

First, I worked on developing my own feed reader, Sigmarootpi Times, with a newspaper-like theme. If you have visited my blog earlier, you know my affinity towards news websites. For first-time viewers you can read here what I am talking about. Anyway, it took a couple of hours to develop everything from scratch and tweak here and there, but overall Claude did a good job. It's built on Node.js and even has a login screen which remembers the user for thirty days.

It is still far from being perfect but I got something reasonably close to my expectation. What I like about the design is a lot of graphics, which draw my attention to headlines. I can skim through hundreds of articles and read what I like. The feed reader keeps a history of what I have read and what I have not. It also pulls new posts every six hours, so I get a fresh newspaper four times a day. I have added a video column too where I can see newly posted YouTube videos from subscribed channels and watch them directly without opening YouTube. There is a dark mode as well.

Overall, I was quite satisfied with it. But after using it for a couple of weeks, I found that this method has a downside. The news website design utilizes graphics heavily which are in abundance in news posts but scarce in blog posts. Naturally, I was opening graphic-based articles more compared to posts with mundane headlines--Robert Birming wrote about the same issue that blogs need more photos. This kills the whole point for which I designed Sigmarootpi Times as I prefer to read blog posts over news articles.

So, I moved to my second idea--modifying FreshRSS by developing its plugins. Again, I used Claude for it. I mentioned above that I wanted FreshRSS to act as a link aggregator and not as a feed reader. So, I took inspiration from Hacker News design and built an extension which modify FreshRSS theme.

The main working of FreshRSS is still the same except the result of direct click on a new post. Now clicking on the link opens the entry on the original website, and not in the native reader. In case I want to read a post in FreshRSS, I have added a "note icon" which opens the entry in native reader.

After modifying FreshRSS, I found myself using it more for blog post reading. On the main page, I only see a list of posts from my subscribed feeds with no eye-catching features (graphics). So, they all look the same and I can go through them one by one.

What I learnt from this experiment is that for skimming through a large number of feeds, Sigmarootpi Times is a better choice. After all, news websites are designed to make you click on something, if not everything. However, for reading every single new post a distraction-free reader is more suitable. I will be using both.

I am not sharing Sigmarootpi Times's code here as I am shy about it. But if you are interested, you can ask for it. For FreshRSS extension you can download it from GitHub.

item.title: Re: No, I dont want you to summarise the page
item.description:
Hyde and Kev wrote about their dislike for summarize-option provided by LLM agents in almost all popular software and search engines. I completely agree with them.

Although, their focus is on online writing and privacy, I see the same problem when reading a scientific article. This morning, I was attending a scientific talk where the presenter was showing his article in Adobe Reader, and Adobe, annoyingly, kept showing a pop-up at bottom to summarize the article. What the heck.

I don't understand why a popular reader needs to push pop-ups of summarizing text without asking its users whether they want it or not. Adobe reader is already a bloated software, and adding Ask AI option in the top secondary bar with colourful icon makes it even more ugly and distracting. Furthermore, how can one believe the answers of a LLM agent especially if they are not the most accurate ones like GPT and Claude. In the end, reading a research paper will become even more frustrating if a LLM is used there. I know this because it pisses me off most of the time when I try to use a LLM.

item.title: I built my own music collection and why you should too
item.description:
Till my late twenties (now I am in my early thirties) I used to listen to music regularly. During my teen years it was on a bulky cassette player or a Walkman, or on the radio. In later years I switched to portable music players and then to mobile/smartphones. I still remember those moments vividly when I used to get excited about a new song and then go to a nearby music shop to get a copy of it. Each time I needed to ask my mother for the money, and request her not to tell my father ;).

As I get older, I started listening to music less and less. I do not know whether it was really a growing-up thing or I just got overwhelmed by technology, especially the arrival of online services. I enjoyed the music till I had keypad phones but later there were too many things in on my (smart)phones.

It is hard to find the culprit. And, it's not that I have not used iTunes, Spotify and YouTube subscriptions. I have tried them many times but their auto-suggestion feature was not always good. Often times, after finishing my selected playlist, they played shitty songs and killed the whole vibe. The energy required to skip multiple songs and pick a suitable one was too much. Each time I got overwhelmed and canceled my subscription within a month or two.

Overall my music enthusiasm decreased with time, and I accepted it. However, last year after reading many blog posts, especially by Cory, I got some motivation for building my own music library, and getting rid of online music services, completely.

Slowly, I started collecting my favorite songs on my home server so that I can listen to them anywhere. I also started listening to the radio more to find new songs. I will spare you from the technical details except that I use Plex for self-hosting the media library.

The easy accessibility and minimal distraction gave a huge boost to my music listening. I found myself listening to my music collection regularly. What surprised me the most is that it became a matter of self-discovery. Each time I found a favorite song, I felt as if I found a piece of me; a Lego block of my emotional being. I never expected that this small experiment would bring such a big change in my life.

Now after a year of this experiment, I can say that keeping precious things close to myself makes me happier, more confident and relaxed. I dance in the shower, vibe with beats at work, and hum around when I am bored, just because I am not lost in never-ending list of available music in the world.

I encourage everyone to try it.

item.title: AI blog question challenge
item.description:
AI is such a hot topic now a days that rarely any day passes when I do not encounter a single post in my blogroll, which is small, only around twenty people. Majority of the posts are rants, or rants about someone else's rant. Is this a rant as well? Despite that, I still love reading your posts. They give me new insights and make me aware of new issues. So please keep doing it.

Most of the posts can be put into three categories: haters, lovers, and neutral. I am happy to confirm that most of you are AI haters like me. I even have less to say about AI lovers and neutral people.

However, one thing is clear: no matter how much we hate AI and the control of big corporations over this technology, it is going to stay. It is a new tool in market and we need to adapt.

So I thought to create a blog challenge--may be you will find it useful as well. I would love to see your answers, especially Ava and Manu. Feel free to post it on your blog.

  1. How was your first experience with AI models?
  2. Do you use AI or are you completely against using it?
  3. Do you have any preference among different models, for example Claude vs ChatGPT? If yes, how do you choose?
  4. What aspect of AI models do you like and what do you not like?
  5. How do you feel about AI generated images? Does it annoy you if someone use them in a blog post?
  6. Internet is flooded with AI slop now, full of generated text, images, audio and videos. How do you filter it from authentic human creation? Do you have a strategy?
  7. Are you hopeful for a better future with A.I. or a dystopian one?
  1. How was your first experience with AI models?

I am a skeptical person, and I heard about ChatGPT around 2024 when I started writing my PhD thesis. At that time I was not impressed because I had seen what machine learning models could do before LLMs got popular. I was neither interested in coding agents nor any text writer. I only wanted to improve my writing skills. So, after proudly finishing the first draft of my thesis, I began using GPT to add literature level complex sentences in my thesis. Many people were already ahead in usage by giving it long original texts, but I did not want to give my whole thesis to it as I was afraid of plagiarism.

  1. Do you use AI or are you completely against using it?

Nowadays I use it daily but mostly as an alternative to a search engine. Fortunately, for my work I do not need it but when I do, I ask for brief suggestions as if it were an assistant. For coding, I tested GPT once, extravagantly, and it made such a mess that now I prefer to do things myself.

  1. Do you have any preference among different models, for example Claude vs ChatGPT? If yes, how do you choose?

I do have preferences for different use cases. For general purposes its easy to go with GPT or Claude. However, by playing around with different available models in the market, I found that Gemini is good for search, Deepseek is good for strong reasoning, and many unpopular small models that can be run on a PC are good enough to solve my daily tasks. Since I do not want to waste energy, I use GPT or Claude for advance work.

Answering the GPT vs. Claude question, I feel a natural liking toward Claude.

  1. What aspect of AI models do you like and what do you not like?

Honestly, I have more dislike toward AI models, despite of their ability to solve complex problems that can be solved by humans. Even though I use AI daily, I do not find anything good in it. Yes, it save my time but it also leave me dissatisfied with the work.

What I particularly dislike is that the conversation with it feels like talking to a charlatan. Confronting it still reveals its machine mind, or gotcha, and yet it tells lies with so much confidence.

  1. How do you feel about AI generated images? Does it annoy you if someone use them in a blog post?

I am fine with their usage in creative ways. Of course, I do not want to read a blog post written by AI, but if you add something AI generated which can convey your emotions I will not mind. But please mention always that it is AI generated so that someone will not feel cheated.

  1. Internet is flooded with AI slop now, full of generated text, images, audio and videos. How do you filter it from authentic human creation? Do you have a strategy?

Oh! A hard question. I am not smart enough to defeat AI slop. Neither do I have time to deal with it. So I simply walk away. I am not on social media so I do not see much slop. This preserves my critical energy for the content sent by my closed circle.

Blogs can also be a source of AI slop, but I only spend my time on blogs run by genuine people. That said, it takes time to build trust which is easier if you communicate with the author via Fediverse or email.

One trick to recognize AI slop is to spot the struggle of AI models in simulating physics. This works for now and it might improve later.

  1. Are you hopeful for a better future with A.I. or a dystopian one?

It's clear that this tech is not going anywhere. So I do hope that after norms and regulations are made we will see a shift in its use case. There are more crucial problems of privacy and surveillance by the government itself, but I do hope that it will still be in favor of the state, and not of any corporation.

--

I have no idea how many people wrote about this challenge. But those I find are here:

  1. Cesar Agguire
  2. Manu Moreale
  3. Ava
  4. Haewyr
  5. Kev Quirk
  6. Thomas Rigbi
  7. Bongo Twisty
  8. Firesphere.dev

item.title: WV15-Carspreading is real and we should not encourage it
item.description:
Hello. Good morning. It's Monday, and I am sitting in my office figuring out what I want to do today—experiments, data analysis, or computer modelling. I am more inclined to analyse the data for now.

The reason is laziness, which has something to do with last night. I went to bed late, around 2 a.m., when my regular time is around 10–11 p.m. Since it was Sunday, I took a nap in the afternoon. Then in the evening, when I was not feeling sleepy, I started searching for second-hand cars because I need to buy one. My current one, an old Hyundai i10, is getting older and its registration will expire in three years. So despite it being a nice car, I needed to sell it. If I don't do it, it will go to scrap after the registration expires. It's time to move on.

Last evening I was checking reviews of different Indian cars. Interestingly, what I found is that people tend to choose what is popular even when it's an expensive business. Most people do not want to take risks, so they buy what others have tried. Not much creativity, eh.

I, on the other hand, think differently because I like to personalize things a lot. I usually give more time than usual to decide, but once I decide I accept whatever comes, which often results in a peaceful and memorable experience.

Nowadays, all around the world, the size of cars is increasing. There is a specific term for it: carspreading. Of course not everyone is happy about it because bigger cars need more space. But most customers love it because it's all about how much you get in return for your money. So bigger is better.

In this segment of bigger cars, there is this weird combination of hatchback and SUV known as a crossover SUV. Why not a crossover hatchback? Well, again, bigger (toward SUV) is better. Ironically, these cars look more like hatchbacks than SUVs.

To be honest, I am not against SUVs—I do love them—but I am not sure about this crossover. These fake SUVs look bigger from outside while inside the engine is still from a hatchback.

In the Indian market, there are a few models below 10 lakhs (10k euros), but there are not many choices in this segment. So it's hard to decide which one I like. I usually like unique things, which has something to do with social interaction. Unique things make it hard for people to comment because they do not fall into familiar categories, so people hesitate to comment. Of course the downside is that it draws attention, which I often ignore.

Anyway, the conclusion of the car hunt was none. I still could not decide. There was none in the price segment I want to buy, so I was frustrated. Then, due to looking so long at my Mac/phone screen, I got a headache. I still have it.

I feel the choice paradox is at play. I feel like giving up the car hunt and taking some time to digest the information. In India, Nissan and Renault have a smaller secondhand market, while Tata, Hyundai, and Suzuki are popular, so the latter ones are easy to buy and sell. Feature-wise, Renault and Nissan both are competitive, so their cars look cool, loaded with many nice features. However, the catch is that these features often come in upper models, which increases the price and puts these cars at the border of my budget and therefore less appealing.

Okay, I feel humiliated enough about my English, so I am finishing my target today. See you next time.

item.title: WV14-Writing doubts and inspiration
item.description:
From yesterday I have been feeling a doubtful state of mind related to blogging and writing. I feel as if I have no important words to say, my opinions are limited, and most of the bloggers I follow are just complaining about someone or something in their posts. There are a few exceptions, such as Appadict or Andrew's linkdumps, which have a certain theme, but for others there is nothing new to write. The most common topics of complaint are AI and social media.

This week I wrote two posts but never published them because they contain micro thoughts on different topics, or what I am feeling at the moment of writing. There is no coherent structure in them, which might not be good for a reader if I post them. Wait a minute - am I thinking about the reader now?

This chain of thought led me to read my earlier posts from last year. I found that I wrote on a variety of topics, from my career struggles to books on philosophy and the supernatural. But now I feel empty and underconfident. My mind does not want to express anything, or if it does the topic seems mundane and unimportant.

To resolve this problem I visited the blog of Visa, who, to my knowledge, started posting 1000-word vomits a day back in 2012. I dug through the older posts, mostly the first twenty or thirty, to see how his attitude changed with the everyday struggle of doing the word vomit. What I found is a difference between my challenge and his. He never claimed he was going to do it every day. His plan was to do a thousand entries with a thousand words each. He is still doing it after more than ten years.

While what I did was force myself to write for fifty days in a row, which I now think was too much. Now I can see it.

I was also checking his mental health by analyzing the data from his blog. This method is common in the physics community to study a complex system. What I did was take all of Visa's posts and ask Claude to plot usage of positive words every few months. By positive words I mean happy, healthy, growth, beauty, etc. Interestingly, this would have taken me quite a while if needed to be done by myself, but Claude did it in a few minutes. I saw how his posting frequency changed over time and how, in different phases of life, he started using different words. For instance, in his late twenties to early thirties he started using words like beauty, calmness, and peace.

However, to be honest, I felt a bit guilty for looking into someone else's mind. Sorry, Visa. I might have a similar pattern, and even though it feels uncomfortable that someone can spot a hole in my understanding, I feel OK with it. A contradiction, right?

Reading his entries gave me a boost of motivation. I feel I can also write in a similar way and not think much. The only difference is English being my second language. I do not think I can write as fast as Visa did. When I try, I make so many mistakes that I feel shy.

Anyway, I finished today's target of five hundred words. See you next time.

item.title: WV13-Distracted mind and browser hunt
item.description:
In those days when I have no fixed goal to achieve, my mind wanders a lot. As a result, I end up tinkering with my blog or doing random internet searches. I think it's not bad when there is a weekend, but what bothers me is that I fall into this trap during weekdays.

A distracted mind acts weirdly because it repeats the same thing, which makes it even more distracted. With more repetition, it loses its energy and starts getting frustrated.

Those days when I am focused, I finish my work with calmness and peace. There is a sense of accomplishment after the focus mode. A similar feeling can be observed after a workout session. I feel calm after that as well.

So it's an irony that a mind that seeks calmness acts in contradiction to the very thing (focus) that can give it calmness.

--

My search for a browser that can be used both on Linux and Mac systems and does not prey on my data is still on. Previously I was using Safari on Mac and Chrome on both Mac and Linux. Safari was a good browser for me until I was limited to Apple. For moving from one platform to another, I was using Chrome.

However, both have issues. Safari is a good candidate for those in the Apple ecosystem. Chrome, on the other hand, is universally available and can be used in most of the common OSes, but it is known for privacy issues.

A couple of months ago I heard about Orion browser from Kagi. They built an open-source browser for better privacy based on the Safari engine. Initially, I liked it when I was using it on my Mac and iPhone, but the problem of using it on Linux was (and still is) there.

Orion works great on Mac and has features similar to Safari, such as syncing its data via iCloud to my iPhone. However, similar to Safari, it also limits you to the Apple ecosystem. The Kagi team is working on its Linux build and launched a beta version, but it is very buggy. So I need to wait until its stable Linux version is launched.

Yesterday, I saw a post from Loren where they mentioned Helium browser and how nice it is. So I thought I'd give it a shot.

What I found is that it is an open-source version of Chromium and is strongly focused on privacy. Since its engine is based on Chrome, it is available for all three common systems: Linux, Mac, and Windows. Even though it is in beta, it's way ahead in development compared to Orion. I tested it on both Mac and Linux, and it's working fine on both systems. So I have no complaints except some frustration related to the initial struggle of installing extensions in the Mac version.

Design-wise it is also nice, as it gives me the feeling of using Safari, but it's actually a minimalist version of Chromium. So overall it seems a solid option. However, compared with Orion, I feel that there should be a way in Helium to sync history—maybe there is, I am just not aware of it.

This browser is so privacy-focused that you need a third-party password manager and history manager to sync your data from one system to another. Everything stays local.

I am using BitWarden and Hister as a password manager and history manager, respectively, but I am unsure whether it can make everyone happy. If you use Google's default services, then you need to install extensions from Google, which makes this browser pointless.

For me, it is a good solution until the Kagi team succeeds in building Orion for Linux.

item.title: WV12-Limit of critical-thinking
item.description:
I am ruminating over my writing style, especially after I restarted the word-vomit series. What I feel is that my style of writing a post and word-vomit is very similar. I share my experiences in both types of posts. Moreover, despite calling a post word-vomit, I am usually careful about the texts. So it is never really a word-vomit.

The key difference between my writing of a post and a word-vomit is that a post focuses on one theme, while word-vomit can have two to three chains of thought.

This creates a dilemma in naming the current series, word-vomit series, where I every time ask myself whether today's post is a word-vomit or a regular post. I can also call it small-thoughts, similar to what Ava does.

Anyway, let's jump to today's topic.

--

After so much hard thinking, I decided to talk about writing movie and book reviews and maintaining a digital garden. One of my close friends today asked me why I do not discuss scientific topics or ideas on my blog, especially when my introductory line of the blog—just before the recent design change—was related to the topics of philosophy and physics.

He was right to point this out, as I myself asked the same question many times. The reason, I think, is my limited energy to think critically. When I started the blog one and a half years ago, I was planning to do many things. I was excited to try many new ideas in addition to just blogging, such as making my own wiki (a digital garden of my research work) and writing reviews of the books I read or movies I watch.

Among all these ideas, I managed to create and maintain a digital garden, where I regularly update old entries and add new ones, which are mostly based on research articles I read. I try to add new theories of pattern formation physics or new patterns I spot somewhere. You can have a look if you are curious about pattern formation.

I also tried to write reviews, but I could not keep up. The review posts became more like my comment posts instead of reviews. The reason was that I overestimated the amount of critical thinking I can do in a single day. I did not consider whether I would have enough energy to write critical reviews of books and movies after a whole day of work.

With time, I realized that it is not feasible to write critical reviews along with blogging and maintaining a digital garden. So now, thinking about writing a blog post on scientific topics adds more mental pressure, especially when my job is doing physics throughout day.

Furthermore, my job is so intensive that after a whole day of critical thinking, my mind is so messed up that it needs a place to express emotions. So, ironically, this blog turned into a personal blog instead of a scientific blog, where I try to express my struggle with ideas, self-doubts, impostor syndrome, and career struggles.
